titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Abraham to David: the Line of Kings (ch. 13–16)
part: ch. 13–16 — Abraham to David: the Line of Kings
about: Abram refuses his father's idols and is called by the one God, is renamed Abraham, and leaves for Salem; the covenant promise includes the coming of the Ark. The kingship then passes from Isaac and Jacob to Judah, since Reuben, the firstborn, forfeits it, and runs down through Perez and the genealogy to David.

sentences.t: ፲ወ፫ ፡ በእንተ ፡ አብርሃም ።
sentences.l: 13. Concerning Abraham
sentences.i: Chapter 13: Concerning Abraham
sentences.n: Chapter heading. Ethiopic numerals: ፲ወ፫ = 10 and 3 = 13 (ወ between numerals is 'and'; ፲ 10, ፫ 3). በእንተ 'concerning' takes the following noun in the construct/accusative. Names: አብራም Abram is the patriarch's name before God renames him (ch. 14); አብርሃም Abraham afterwards. The heading already uses the later name for the whole story.

sentences.t: ወወለደ ፡ ታራ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ወሰመዮ ፡ አብራም ፤
sentences.l: And-he-begot Terah a-son, and-he-named-him Abram;
sentences.i: Terah begot a son, and named him Abram;
sentences.n: ወ- 'and' opens almost every unit; I will not repeat that. ወለደ 'he begot' is a simple perfect (3ms); ታራ Terah is the subject, ወልደ 'a son' the object (accusative ending -ä). ወሰመዮ = ወ + ሰመየ 'he named' + -o 'him'. UNCERTAIN: the clause order 'begot Terah a son, and named him Abram' reads a little abruptly, and who does the naming is only implied (Terah). I take it as printed; Genesis 11:26 names Terah's sons, and the Kebra Nagast simply compresses it.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ ዓመተ ፡ ለአኮ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ታራ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሢጥ ፡ ጣዖተ ፤
sentences.l: And-when was to-him 12 years, sent-him his-father Terah that he-sell idols;
sentences.i: And when he was twelve years old, his father Terah sent him to sell idols;
sentences.n: ሶበ 'when'. ኮነ ሎቱ 'was to him' is the Geʿez way to say 'he had / he was' (ሎቱ = ለ- + -ቱ 'to him'); ፲ወ፪ ዓመተ '12 years' (10 and 2), the noun in the accusative -ä. ለአኮ is read as ለአከ 'he sent' + -o 'him' (root l-ʾ-k; the spelling ለአኮ is read as ለአከ + -o, UNCERTAIN but fits the sense). ከመ ይሢጥ 'that he sell': ከመ + the subjunctive (ይሢጥ, 3ms) expresses purpose. This ከመ + subjunctive pattern recurs constantly. ጣዖት 'idol' (I do not know the word's origin).

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ አብራም ፡ ዝሰ ፡ ኢኮነ ፡ አምላክ ፡ ዘያድኅን ፤
sentences.l: And-said Abram: 'This indeed is-not a-god that-saves';
sentences.i: and Abram said, 'This is no god that saves';
sentences.n: ይቤ 'he said' (defective verb, ይቤሎ 'he said to him', ይቤሎሙ 'he said to them'). ኢኮነ 'is not / was not' (ኢ- negation + ኮነ). ዘያድኅን = ዘ- 'which, who' + ያድኅን 'he saves' (causative አድኅነ). ዝሰ is ዝ 'this' (the short masculine demonstrative, used alongside ዝንቱ) + the contrastive enclitic -ሰ ('this one, for its part'); l shows the -ሰ as 'indeed' and i leaves its force light. -ሰ is a particle you will see again (አንተሰ, መንግሥትሰ).

sentences.t: ወወሰደ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሢጥ ፡ ጣዖተ ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዞ ፡ አቡሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-took-away that he-sell idols as his-father commanded-him;
sentences.i: and he took them away to sell them, as his father had commanded him;
sentences.n: ወሰደ 'he took away, carried off' (understood object: the idols, which the next clause names). በከመ 'as, according as' (በ- 'in' + ከመ). አዘዞ = አዘዘ 'he commanded' + -o 'him'. Verb-final object suffixes (-o him, -omu them) are a pattern to watch.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ይሠይጥ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ቦኑ ፡ ዘትሣየጡ ፡ ዘኢያድኅን ፡ አምላክ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ ወእብን ፡ ወኀጺን ፡ ወብርት ፡ ዘገብሮ ፡ እደ ፡ ኬንያ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-them to-those who he-sells to-them: 'Is-it (so) that-what you-buy, which-not saves, (is) a-god — wood and-stone and-iron and-bronze(?) — that made-it the-hand-of the-craftsman(?);
sentences.i: And he said to those to whom he sold, 'Is what you buy, which cannot save, a god — wood and stone and iron and bronze — which a craftsman's hand made?
sentences.n: ለእለ ይሠይጥ ሎሙ 'to those to whom he sells (to them)': እለ 'those who' is the plural relative, and the resumptive ሎሙ 'to them' repeats it, as Geʿez often does. ቦኑ = ቦ 'is there' + -ኑ (question particle): 'is it so that…?', here a rhetorical question. ዘትሣየጡ 'which you buy' (root ś-y-ṭ, as in ይሠይጥ above and ተሣይጦ below). The list ዕፅ ወእብን ወኀጺን ወብርት: ዕፅ wood, እብን stone, ኀጺን iron; ብርት I take as 'bronze', as in ch. 9–12 (ወብርት); the exact metal is uncertain without Dillmann. ዘገብሮ እደ ኬንያ: ገብሮ 'made it'; ኬንያ is the craftsman/fashioner word (the same noun as ወኬንያሃ 'her fashioner' in ch. 1); እደ is the construct of the singular እድ 'hand' (plural እደው, as in ch. 13's ሰፍሐ እደዊሁ), so 'the hand of a craftsman' agrees with the singular verb ገብሮ; the -o 'it' is resumptive for ዘ. Echoes the prophetic polemic against idols (Psalm 115:4; Isaiah 44).

sentences.t: ወአበይዎ ፡ ተሣይጦ ፡ ለአብራም ፡ እስመ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ አርኰሶሙ ፡ ለግልፈዋተ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ያአትዎሙ ፡ ተግሕሠ ፡ እምፍኖት ፡ ወአንበሮሙ ፡ ወነጸሮሙ ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-refused-him buying from-Abram, because he-himself had-defiled the-carved-images-of his-father; and-while he-was-bringing-them-in he-turned-aside from-the-road and-set-them and-looked-at-them and-said to-them:
sentences.i: But they refused to buy from Abram, because he himself had defiled his father's carved images; and while he was bringing them in, he turned off the road, set them down, looked at them, and said to them,
sentences.n: UNCERTAIN, several points. ወአበይዎ ተሣይጦ ለአብራም: አበይዎ is the 3rd plural perfect አበዩ 'they refused' + -o 'him', with the infinitive ተሣይጦ 'buying'; ለአብራም either repeats the -o ('him, Abram') or gives 'from Abram'. The verb is plural, so the buyers are the subject: 'they refused to buy from Abram'. ለግልፈዋተ: ለ- marks the object again after the verb with -ሙ. ለሊሁ 'he himself' (emphatic). አርኰሶሙ ለግልፈዋተ: አርኰሰ 'defile, dishonour' (the verb of ch. 16, used of Reuben); ግልፈዋት is plural of a word for carved images (ግልፍ 'carved/graven') — the exact word is not certain to me. ያአትዎሙ 'he brings them in' (አአተወ, causative of አተወ 'enter'), after እንዘ 'while'. ተግሕሠ 'he turned aside'. Sequence of perfects: አንበሮሙ 'he set them', ነጸሮሙ 'he looked at them'.

sentences.t: ቦኑ ፡ ዘትክሉ ፡ ገቢረ ፡ ዘእሴአለክሙ ፡ አነ ፡ ይእዜ ፡ እመ ፡ ትክሉ ፡ አብልዑኒ ፡ ኅብስተ ፡ አው ፡ አስትዩኒ ፡ ማየ ፤
sentences.l: 'Is-it (so) that-you-can do what I-ask-you, I, now? If you-can, feed-me bread or give-me-to-drink water!'
sentences.i: 'Can you do what I ask of you, now? If you can, feed me bread or give me water to drink!'
sentences.n: ዘእሴአለክሙ = ዘ- 'what' + እሴአል 'I ask' + -ክሙ 'you (pl.)'. Imperatives with the pronoun -ኒ 'me': አብልዑኒ 'feed me' (አብልዐ), አስትዩኒ 'give me to drink' (አስተየ). ትክሉ 'you (pl.) are able'. The mocking test of the idols is a standard Jewish-Christian tale of Abraham.

sentences.t: ወአልቦ ፡ ዘአውሥእዎ ፡ እስመ ፡ አእባን ፡ ወዕፀው ፡ እሙንቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-there-was-not (one) who they-answered-him, for stones and-trees they;
sentences.i: But no one answered him, for they were stones and trees.
sentences.n: አልቦ 'there is not / there was no one' (አል- 'not' + ቦ 'there is'). ዘአውሥእዎ 'who answered him' (አውሥአ 'answer'): the verb is 3rd plural, 'they answered him', so the clause is impersonal, 'there was none who they answered him', that is, no one answered him. Plurals: አእባን 'stones' (from እብን), ዕፀው 'trees, wood' (from ዕፅ) — 'broken' plurals made by changing the internal vowel pattern, common in Geʿez. እሙንቱ 'they' (masc. pl.).

sentences.t: ወጸዐሎሙ ፡ ወፀረፈ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፡ ወኢነበብዎ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-was-wroth-at-them and-reviled over-them, and-not-they-spoke-to-him;
sentences.i: He was furious with them and reviled them, and they did not speak to him.
sentences.n: UNCERTAIN: ጸዐሎሙ — I read ጸዐለ 'be angry with, hate' + -omu 'them'; the root is not one I can check. ፀረፈ ላዕሌሆሙ 'he reviled / blasphemed against them' (ላዕለ 'over, against' + -ሆሙ). ኢነበብዎ 'they did not speak to him' (ነበበ, with -o). Note ኢ- placed before the verb as the negative, with ወ- before it.

sentences.t: ወቦ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ጸፍዖ ፡ ወቦ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ረገፆ ፡ ወቦ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ወገሮ ፡ ወሰበሮ ፡ በአእባን ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-there-was for-him-who he-slapped-him, and-there-was for-him-who he-kicked-him, and-there-was for-him-who he-pelted-him and-broke-him with-stones; and-said-to-them:
sentences.i: Some he slapped, some he kicked, and some he pelted and broke with stones; and he said to them,
sentences.n: ቦ ለዘ 'there is for him who' = 'some (one)… some (another)'. The three verbs: ጸፍዖ 'he slapped him', ረገፆ 'he kicked him', ወገሮ 'he pelted him'; ሰበሮ 'he broke him'; the idols are treated as persons, hence the -o 'him' suffixes.

sentences.t: እመሰ ፡ ኢታድኅኑ ፡ ርእስክሙ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ገፍዐክሙ ፡ ወኢታሐሥሙ ፡ ለዘ ፡ አሕሠመ ፡ ለክሙ ፡ በአይቴ ፡ ትሰመዩ ፡ አማልክተ ፤
sentences.l: 'If-indeed not you-save yourselves from-him-who struck-you, and-not you-requite him-who harmed to-you, by-what are-you-called gods?
sentences.i: 'If you cannot save yourselves from the one who strikes you, and cannot pay back the one who harms you, in what sense are you called gods?
sentences.n: እመሰ 'if indeed' (እመ 'if' + -ሰ). ርእስክሙ 'your heads' = idiomatic 'yourselves' (ርእስ 'head' is the Geʿez reflexive). ገፍዐ 'strike, oppress'. UNCERTAIN: ታሐሥሙ / አሕሠመ — both seem to come from one root (ḥ-ś-m, a verb of harming), so the sense would be 'you do not harm him who harmed you', that is, you cannot pay back; I cannot check the root. በአይቴ 'by what / how' (lit. 'in where'). ትሰመዩ 'you are called' (passive of ሰመየ), with a second accusative አማልክተ 'gods' (plural of አምላክ).

sentences.t: ወከንቱ ፡ እለ ፡ ያመልኩክሙ ፡ ወአንሰ ፡ አስተሐቀርኩክሙ ፡ ወኢትኩኑኒ ፡ አምላኪየ ፡ ወአርአየ ፡ ገጾ ፡ ለምሥራቅ ፡ ወሰፍሐ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወይቤ ፤
sentences.l: Vain (are) those-who worship-you; as-for-me I-despise-you, and-be-not-to-me my-god.' And-he-showed his-face to-the-east and-spread his-hands and-said:
sentences.i: Vain are those who worship you. As for me, I despise you; do not be my god.' And he turned his face to the east, spread out his hands, and said,
sentences.n: ከንቱ 'vain, empty'. ያመልኩክሙ 'they worship you' (አምለከ). አንሰ = አነ 'I' + -ሰ ('as for me'). አስተሐቀርኩክሙ 'I despised you' (perfect, 1sg). ኢትኩኑኒ አምላኪየ 'be not for me my god' — negative imperative of ኮነ with -ኒ. አምላኪየ 'my god': አምላክ + the 1sg suffix -የ, joined by a linking vowel (the ኪ is the noun's own final ክ with that vowel, not a separate suffix). አርአየ ገጾ 'he showed his face' = turned it. ምሥራቅ 'east' (the sunrise). ሰፍሐ እደዊሁ 'he spread his hands' (እደ 'hand', plural እደው).

sentences.t: አምላኪየሰ ፡ ኩነኒ ፡ አንተ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ፈጣሬ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ወምድር ፡ ፈጣሬ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ወወርኅ ፡ ፈጣሬ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወየብስ ፡ ገባሬ ፡ ሰርጐ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወምድር ፡ ዘያስተርኢ ፡ ወዘኢያስተርኢ ፡ ገባሬ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ኩነኒ ፡ አምላኪየ ፡ ወኪያከ ፡ ተአመንኩ ፡ ወባዕደሰ ፡ አልብየ ፡ ዘእትአመን ፡ ዘእንበሌከ ፡ እምዮም ፡ ወእምዝ ፡ አስተርአዮ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ዘእሳት ፡ ዘይነድድ ፡ ወፈርሀ ፡ አብራም ፡ ወወድቀ ፡ በገጹ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድር ፤
sentences.l: 'As-for-my-god, be-to-me you, O-Lord, creator-of heavens and-earth, creator-of sun and-moon, creator-of sea and-dry-land, maker-of adornment-of heaven and-earth, that-which appears and-that-which not-appears, maker-of all; be-to-me my-god. And-you I-believed-in; and-another-indeed there-is-not-to-me in-whom-I-believe, apart-from-you, from-today.' And-then appeared-to-him a-chariot of-fire which burns; and-feared Abram, and-fell on-his-face to the-ground;
sentences.i: 'As for my God — be my God, you, O Lord, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Creator of sun and moon, Creator of sea and dry land, Maker of the adornment of heaven and earth, of what is seen and what is unseen, Maker of all; be my God. In you I have believed, and I have no other in whom to believe besides you, from this day.' And after this a chariot of fire, blazing, appeared to him; and Abram was afraid and fell with his face to the ground;
sentences.n: A prayer made of construct chains, the book's favourite pattern: ፈጣሬ ሰማያት 'creator-of heavens', ፈጣሬ ፀሐይ 'creator-of sun', ገባሬ ሰርጐ ሰማይ 'maker-of adornment-of heaven'. The head noun ends in -ä (ፈጣሬ, ገባሬ), the construct/accusative form, and the next noun follows without a linking word. Here they are in direct address, so 'O Creator of…'. እግዚኦ is እግዚእ 'lord' + the vocative -ኦ, 'O Lord'. ኩነኒ 'be to me' (imperative ኩን + -ኒ). ሰርጕ 'adornment, ordering' — the sense 'ornament' is my reading; UNCERTAIN. ዘያስተርኢ ወዘኢያስተርኢ 'what appears and what does not' (visible and invisible; cf. the creed, Colossians 1:16). ኪያከ ተአመንኩ: ኪያከ is the object form 'you' ('it is you whom'), ተአመነ 'believe' takes the accusative here. ባዕደሰ አልብየ 'as for another, I have not' (ባዕድ 'other'); ዘእትአመን 'in whom I might believe' (subjunctive). ዘእንበሌከ 'apart from you'. አስተርአዮ = አስተርአየ 'he appeared, showed himself' (the Ct stem of ርእየ, the same stem as ያስተርኢ above) + -o 'to him'; ሰረገላ 'chariot' (cf. 2 Kings 2:11); ፈርሀ 'he feared'.

sentences.t: ወአንሥኦ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ኢትፍራህ ፡ ቁም ፡ ርቱዐ ፡ ወአእተተ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ፍርሀተ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-he-raised-him and-said-to-him: 'Do-not-fear; stand upright'; and-removed from-him fear. . . .
sentences.i: He raised him up and said to him, 'Do not be afraid; stand upright'; and he took the fear from him. . . .
sentences.n: No subject is stated; the verbs are 3rd masculine singular, and I take the one in the chariot to be meant (UNCERTAIN: ሰረገላ is itself masculine, so the chariot is a grammatical possibility). አንሥኦ 'he raised him' (አንሥአ). ኢትፍራህ 'do not fear' (ኢ- + subjunctive/jussive ትፍራህ, 2ms), the usual 'fear not' formula of Scripture. ቁም 'stand'. ርቱዐ 'upright' (accusative -ä, adverbial). ፍርሀተ 'fear' (accusative of ፍርሀት); አእተተ 'he removed' with እምኔሁ 'from him' (እም + ኔ- + -ሁ). The ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ run marks the end of the chapter.

sentences.t: ፲ወ፬ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ኪዳነ ፡ አብርሃም ።
sentences.l: 14. Concerning covenant-of Abraham
sentences.i: Chapter 14: Concerning the Covenant of Abraham
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲ወ፬ = 14. ኪዳነ 'covenant-of' is in the construct (accusative) after በእንተ; አብርሃም follows with no linking particle. From here the patriarch is አብርሃም Abraham in the heading, though the narrative still says አብራም until God changes the name.

sentences.t: ወተናገሮ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይቤሎ ፤
sentences.l: And-spoke-with-him God and-said-to-him:
sentences.i: And God spoke with him and said to him,
sentences.n: ተናገሮ = ተናገረ 'he spoke' + -o 'to/with him'. እግዚኣብሔር 'God' (lit. 'Lord of the land/world'; the spelling alternates with እግዚአብሔር in this part of the text, as printed).

sentences.t: ኢትፍራህ ፡ እምዮም ፡ ገብርየ ፡ አንተ ፡ ወኣቀውም ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ወምስለ ፡ ዘርእከ ፡ እምድኅሬከ ፡ ወኣበዝኅ ፡ ዘርአከ ፡ ወኣዐቢ ፡ ስምከ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ወኣወርዳ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ኪዳንየ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ በ፯ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ እምድኅሬከ ፡ ወታንሶሱ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዘርእከ ፡ ወትከውን ፡ መድኀኒተ ፡ ለዘመድከ ፤
sentences.l: 'Do-not-fear from-today; my-servant you; and-I-will-establish my-covenant with-you and-with your-seed after-you, and-I-will-multiply your-seed and-I-will-make-great your-name exceedingly; and-I-will-bring-down her, the-ark-of my-covenant, upon earth in 7 generation(s) after-you, and-she-will-walk with your-seed; and-you-will-be saviour for-your-kin;
sentences.i: 'Do not be afraid from this day: you are my servant. I will establish my covenant with you and with your seed after you; I will multiply your seed and make your name very great. And I will bring down the Ark of my covenant upon the earth in seven generations after you, and it will go about with your seed; and you will be a saviour for your kin.
sentences.n: Echoes Genesis 12:2 and 15–17 (covenant, seed, great name). ኣ- (for እ-) on ኣቀውም 'I will establish', ኣበዝኅ 'I will multiply', ኣዐቢ 'I will make great', ኣወርዳ 'I will bring her down' is the 1sg prefix; the verbs are subjunctive used as a future. ኣወርዳ ለታቦተ: the object suffix -ā 'her' (merged into the final -ዳ) anticipates the noun, 'I will bring her down, the ark-of…'. ታቦት is feminine, hence ታንሶሱ 'she will go about' (3fs). UNCERTAIN: ታንሶሱ and ትከውን are each both 3rd feminine ('she', the Ark) and 2nd masculine ('you'); I take the first as the Ark (it goes about with your seed after you) and the second as Abraham ('you will be a saviour'), but the text does not mark the change of subject, and 'she (the Ark) will be a saviour for your kin' is possible. This is the central claim of the book: the Ark of the covenant comes to dwell on earth with Abraham's line. በ፯ ትውልድ: 'in 7 generation' — whether 'in the seventh generation' or 'after seven generations' is left open by the grammar; ፯ is a cardinal, not an ordinal, so I translate 'in seven generations'. መድኀኒተ 'saviour' (accusative as predicate); ዘመድ 'kin'.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ እፌኑ ፡ ቃልየ ፡ ለመድኀኒተ ፡ አዳም ፡ ወደቂቁ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወይእዜኒ ፡ እሉ ፡ አዝማዲከ ፡ ዐላዊያን ፡ ወአበዩ ፡ አምልኮትየ ፡ በርትዕ ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him I-will-send my-word for-salvation-of Adam and-his-children until for-ever. And-now these your-kinsmen (are) unjust, and-they-refused my-worship in-uprightness;
sentences.i: After him I will send my Word for the salvation of Adam and his children for ever. And now, these kinsmen of yours are unjust, and have refused my worship in uprightness.
sentences.n: ቃልየ 'my Word' — the Logos, i.e. Christ; Adam and his descendants are the object of salvation (the book's framing, see ch. 1). እምድኅሬሁ 'after him' = እም + ድኅሬ 'back, behind' + -ሁ. እፌኑ 'I will send' (1sg subjunctive, ፈነወ). እስከ ለዓለም 'unto for-ever'. ወይእዜኒ 'and now' (-ኒ is the particle 'also, then'). ዐላዊያን 'unjust ones' (from ዐላዊ, plural -ያን). አበዩ 'they refused' (አበየ, 3pl). አምልኮትየ 'my worship'.

sentences.t: ወአንተሰ ፡ ዕለት ፡ እምዕለት ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያስሕቱከ ፡ ነዓ ፡ ፃእ ፡ እምዛቲ ፡ ምድር ፡ ምድረ ፡ አበዊከ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድር ፡ ዘኣርእየከ ፡ አነ ፡ ወእሁቦሙ ፡ ለዘርእከ ፡ እምድኅሬከ ፡ ወሰገደ ፡ አብራም ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወተአዘዘ ፡ ለአምላኩ ፤
sentences.l: But-you, day from-day, lest they-lead-you-astray: come, go-out from-this land, land-of your-fathers, to the-land which I-will-show-you, I; and-I-will-give-them to-your-seed after-you.' And-bowed Abram to-God and-obeyed his-God;
sentences.i: But you — day after day, lest they lead you astray — come, go out from this land, the land of your fathers, to the land which I will show you; and I will give it to your seed after you.' And Abram bowed down to God and obeyed his God;
sentences.n: The call of Genesis 12:1. ወአንተሰ 'but you' (-ሰ again: contrast). ዕለት እምዕለት 'day after day' (lit. 'a day from a day'). ከመ ኢያስሕቱከ 'that they not lead you astray' (ከመ + negated subjunctive; አስሐተ 'lead astray'). ነዓ 'come!' ፃእ 'go out!'. ምድረ አበዊከ 'land-of your-fathers' (construct + -ከ). ዘኣርእየከ 'which I will show you'. እሁቦሙ 'I will give them' (UNCERTAIN: -ሙ is plural 'them' where the sense is the one land; I render 'it'). ሰገደ 'he bowed down' (+ ለ-); ተአዘዘ 'he obeyed'.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ስምከ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ሰላመ ፡ ወዐርገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰማያት ፨
sentences.l: And-said-to-him: 'Let-be your-name Abraham'; and-he-gave-him peace and-ascended into heavens.
sentences.i: And he said to him, 'Let your name be Abraham'; and he gave him peace and went up into heaven.
sentences.n: Genesis 17:5, the renaming አብራም → አብርሃም: from here Abraham. ይኩን 'let it be' (jussive of ኮነ). ወሀቦ 'he gave him'; ሰላመ 'peace' (a farewell blessing). ሰማያት 'heavens' is a plural form with a singular sense in English. The ፨ here ends the unit but not the paragraph.

sentences.t: ወአብርሃምኒ ፡ አተወ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ማኅደሩ ፡ ወነሥኣ ፡ ለሳራ ፡ ብእሲቱ ፡ ወወፅአ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ኢይትመየጥ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወእሞ ፡ ወቤቶ ፡ ወአዝማዲሁ ፡ ወመነነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-Abraham, for his part, entered into his-dwelling and-took Sarah his-wife and-went-out, not turning-back (to) his-father and-his-mother and-his-house and-his-kinsmen, and-renounced (them) for-the-sake-of God;
sentences.i: And Abraham, for his part, went into his dwelling, took Sarah his wife and went out, without turning back to his father and his mother and his house and his kinsmen; and he renounced them for the sake of God;
sentences.n: አብርሃምኒ: -ኒ here is the particle 'also, for his part' marking a new subject. አተወ 'he entered'. ነሥኣ ለሳራ 'he took her, Sarah' (verb carries the -a object, followed by ለ + noun: the usual doubling). እንዘ ኢይትመየጥ 'while not turning back' (እንዘ + imperfect = circumstantial 'without…ing'). መነነ 'he renounced, forsook' (as a monk renounces the world). The book takes Abraham's departure as a model of renunciation.

sentences.t: ወበጽሐ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሳሌም ፡ ወኀደረ ፡ ህየ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ በጽድቅ ፡ ወኢተዐደወ ፡ እምትእዛዙ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-he-reached into city-of Salem and-dwelt there and-reigned in-righteousness, and-not-transgressed from-his-commandment of-God;
sentences.i: He reached the city of Salem and lived there and reigned in righteousness, and did not transgress the commandment of God;
sentences.n: ሀገረ ሳሌም 'city-of Salem' (construct). Salem is Melchizedek's city (Genesis 14:18); this book makes Abraham king there — the Kebra Nagast's own presentation of the Abrahamic line as a kingship. ነግሠ 'he reigned' is the book's key verb (cf. ነገሥት 'kings'); watch it recur. ተዐደወ እም- 'transgress (away from)' is the recurrent verb of this part: Isaac and Jacob 'did not transgress', Reuben does. ትእዛዙ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'his-commandment of-God' — the possessive suffix + ለ- is the common way to express a genitive (the 'indirect genitive'); I will not repeat it.

sentences.t: ወእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ባረኮ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ እስከ ፡ አጥረየ ፡ ዐሠርተ ፡ ወሰመንተ ፡ አግብርቲሁ ፡ እለ ፡ ይቀውሙ ፡ ቅድሜሁ ፡ ጽኑዓን ፡ ወምሁራነ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ እለ ፡ ይገብሩ ፡ ፈቃዶ ፡ እለ ፡ ይለብሱ ፡ ዲባጋተ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ወየዐንቁ ፡ በዝጋናተ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ወይቀንቱ ፡ ቅናታተ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ወይትቄጸሉ ፡ አክሊላተ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፤
sentences.l: And-God blessed-him exceedingly, until he-acquired ten and-eight his-servants, who stand before-him, strong and-trained-of war, who do his-will, who wear brocades of-gold, and-wear-at-the-neck with-collars of-gold, and-gird girdles of-gold, and-crown-themselves crowns of-gold;
sentences.i: And God blessed him greatly, until he had acquired eighteen servants, who stood before him, strong men trained in war, who did his will; who wore brocades of gold, put collars of gold about their necks, girded themselves with belts of gold, and were crowned with crowns of gold;
sentences.n: አጥረየ 'he acquired, gained' (root not certain to me). ዐሠርተ ወሰመንተ 'ten and eight' = 18 as printed (not 318); Genesis 14:14 has 318 trained men, and the printed text has no ፫፻ 'three hundred'. A dropped '300' is possible, but I keep 18 as printed and flag it. The relative clauses go with እለ 'who' (pl.): ይቀውሙ 'they stand'. ምሁራነ 'taught, trained' (accusative plural, a participle of መሀረ 'teach'). ዲባጋት 'brocades' (probably a Persian loanword). UNCERTAIN: የዐንቁ በዝጋናተ — የዐንቁ I take as a verb ዐነቀ from ዐንቅ 'neck' ('they put on at the neck'), with በ- 'with' before ዝጋናተ; ዝጋና I take as 'collar, necklace' from that sense. ይቀንቱ ቅናታተ 'they gird girdles' (ቅናት, from ቀነተ 'gird'). ይትቄጸሉ አክሊላተ 'they are crowned with crowns'. The repeated ዘወርቅ 'of gold' (ዘ- + construct): a list pattern.

sentences.t: ወቦሙ ፡ ይመውእ ፡ ፀሮ ፡ ወአዕረፈ ፡ በክብር ፡ በእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወኀየሰ ፡ ወተሞገሰ ፡ እምእለ ፡ ቅድሜሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-with-them he-overcame his-enemy, and-rested in-glory in-God, and-excelled and-was-praised above those before-him;
sentences.i: With them he defeated his enemy, and he rested in glory in God, and he surpassed and was esteemed above those before him;
sentences.n: ይመውእ 'he conquers' (imperfect used as a narrative past in this book); ፀሮ 'his enemy' (ፀር + -ሁ). ቦሙ 'with them' (ቦ- 'in/with' + -ሙ). አዕረፈ በክብር 'he rested in glory': አዕረፈ is also the standard Ethiopic word for dying peacefully (see ch. 15), so 'rested' keeps both senses. ኀየሰ 'he was excellent, he excelled', ተሞገሰ 'he was praised / esteemed' (passive-reflexive of ሞገሰ). እምእለ 'than those who' (እም + እለ): comparative እም- is the same እም- as 'from'.

sentences.t: ኀየሰ ፡ ወከብረ ፡ ወተለዐለ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: He-excelled and-became-glorious and-was-exalted. . . .
sentences.i: He excelled and was honoured and was exalted. . . .
sentences.n: ተለዐለ 'he was exalted' (the ተ- stem of a verb ለዐለ 'be high', from the root of ላዕል 'high, above'); ከብረ 'he was honoured / became glorious' — the verb of the book's title word ክብር 'glory'. A six-fold ፨ ends the chapter.

sentences.t: ፲ወ፭ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወያዕቆብ ።
sentences.l: 15. Concerning Isaac and-Jacob
sentences.i: Chapter 15: Concerning Isaac and Jacob
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲ወ፭ = 15. Names: ይስሐቅ Isaac, ያዕቆብ Jacob (the Geʿez forms are the standard Ethiopic spellings).

sentences.t: ወነግሠ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ኢተዐደወ ፡ እምትእዛዙ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ በነፍሱ ፡ ወበሥጋሁ ፡ ወአዕረፈ ፡ በክብር ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ኢተዐደወ ፡ እምትእዛዙ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-reigned Isaac his-son, and-he-also not-transgressed from-his-commandment of-God, and-was pure in-his-self and-in-his-body, and-rested in-glory. And-reigned Jacob his-son, and-he-also not-transgressed from-his-commandment of-God;
sentences.i: And his son Isaac reigned, and he also did not transgress the commandment of God; he was pure in soul and in body, and he rested in glory. And his son Jacob reigned, and he also did not transgress the commandment of God;
sentences.n: ውእቱኒ 'he also, he for his part' (ውእቱ 'he' + -ኒ) — the formula that carries the succession, 'and he too'. ንጹሕ 'pure, clean'. በነፍሱ ወበሥጋሁ 'in his soul (self) and in his flesh' — ነፍስ here can be 'life, self'. The unit is 20 words; I keep it whole since the two reigns are stated in one frame. Repeated: ወልዱ 'his son', the father-to-son line of kings, and ትእዛዙ ለእግዚኣብሔር, the standard measure of a king's merit in this part.

sentences.t: ወኮነ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ንዋዩ ፡ ወደቂቁ ፡ ወባረኮ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወአዕረፈ ፡ በክብር ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: and-was many his-wealth and-his-sons, and-God blessed-him, and-rested in-glory. . . .
sentences.i: and his wealth and his sons became many, and God blessed him, and he rested in glory. . . .
sentences.n: ኮነ ብዙኅ ንዋዩ ወደቂቁ: 'was many his goods and his sons' — the verb and adjective stay singular before a compound subject. ንዋይ 'goods, wealth' (ንዋዩ = ንዋይ + -ሁ); ደቂቅ 'sons, children' (plural of ወልድ in the sense 'sons'). The eightfold ፨ is the printed run; it ends the chapter.

sentences.t: ፲ወ፮ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሮቤል ።
sentences.l: 16. Concerning Reuben
sentences.i: Chapter 16: Concerning Reuben
sentences.n: Chapter heading; ፲ወ፮ = 16. Name: ሮቤል Reuben, Jacob's firstborn son.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ሮቤል ፡ በኰሩ ፡ ለያዕቆብ ፡ ተዐደወ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወፈለሰት ፡ መንግሥት ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወእምዘርኡ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘአርኰሰ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢርቱዕ ፡ ተዐድዎ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ዘአዘዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him Reuben, his-firstborn of-Jacob, transgressed the-commandment-of God, and-passed the-kingdom from-him and-from-his-seed because-he defiled the-wife-of his-father, since not (was) right the-transgressing (of) the-law which commanded God;
sentences.i: After him, Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, transgressed the commandment of God, and the kingdom passed from him and from his seed, because he defiled his father's wife; for it was not right to transgress the law that God had commanded.
sentences.n: በኰሩ ለያዕቆብ 'his firstborn, Jacob's' (the suffix + ለ- genitive again). ተዐደወ ትእዛዘ 'he transgressed the commandment' — ተዐደወ takes the accusative directly here (elsewhere እም- 'away from'). ፈለሰት 'it moved, passed' is feminine, agreeing with መንግሥት 'kingdom'. Genesis 35:22 and 49:3–4 (Reuben loses the firstborn's rights). ዘአርኰሰ ብእሲተ አቡሁ 'that he defiled the wife of his father'; በእንተ ዘ- 'because of the fact that'. ኢርቱዕ 'not right' (ኢ- + ርቱዕ 'straight, right'), the predicate of a nominal clause. ተዐድዎ I read as the verbal noun of ተዐደወ, 'the transgressing' (compare ተዐዲዎ ማሕላ in ch. 11, and ተሣይጦ in ch. 13): 'it was not right to transgress the law'. UNCERTAIN: the same letters could also be a perfect with -o ('they transgressed it'), but the ch. 11 parallel favours the verbal noun. ዘአዘዘ እግዚኣብሔር 'which commanded God': verb before subject.

sentences.t: ወረገሞ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወተምዖ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ሕጹጸ ፡ እምአኀዊሁ ፡ ወደቂቁ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ዝልጉሳነ ፡ ወዕቡቃነ ፤
sentences.l: And-cursed-him his-father, and-God was-angry-at-him, and-he-became inferior to-his-brothers, and-his-sons became ዝልጉሳን and ዕቡቃን;
sentences.i: His father cursed him, and God was angry with him, and he became inferior to his brothers; and his sons became feeble and contemptible;
sentences.n: ረገሞ 'he cursed him'; ተምዖ 'he was angry with him' (ተምዐ). ሕጹጸ 'lacking, deficient', the predicate accusative after ኮነ; እምአኀዊሁ 'than his brothers' (comparative እም-). UNCERTAIN: ዝልጉሳነ ወዕቡቃነ — two rare plural accusatives that I cannot check without Dillmann; the sense 'feeble, debased' is a guess from context (the sons suffer for the father's sin). They are predicates after ኮኑ 'they became'.

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ በኴር ፡ ተሀይደ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ እኁሁ ፡ ዘይንእስ ፤
sentences.l: And-while he-himself (was) firstborn, was-taken-away the-kingdom from-him, and-reigned Judah his-brother, who (is) younger;
sentences.i: Though he himself was the firstborn, the kingdom was taken away from him, and Judah, his younger brother, reigned;
sentences.n: እንዘ ለሊሁ በኴር 'while he himself (was) firstborn' (a concessive 'although'); the 'to be' verb is left out, as usual in nominal clauses. ተሀይደ 'was taken away' (passive of ሀይደ). ዘይንእስ 'who is small / younger'. Judah is Jacob's fourth son (Genesis 49:8–10, the sceptre of Judah).

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ ተሰምየ ፡ ይሁዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-for-this-reason he-was-named Judah;
sentences.i: and for this reason he was named Judah;
sentences.n: በእንተዝ = በእንተ 'on account of' + ዝ 'this'. ተሰምየ 'was named' (passive of ሰመየ, cf. ወሰመዮ in ch. 13). The text gives a reason but does not spell out the wordplay; I suspect the name is being linked with ተሀይደ 'was taken', but that is my guess, not something the text says.

sentences.t: ወተባረከ ፡ ዘርኡ ፡ ወሠነየ ፡ መንግሥቱ ፡ ወተባረኩ ፡ ደቂቁ ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ፋሬስ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: And-was-blessed his-seed, and-was-fair his-kingdom, and-were-blessed his-sons; and-after-him reigned Perez his-son;
sentences.i: His seed was blessed, his kingdom was fair, and his sons were blessed; and after him his son Perez reigned;
sentences.n: ተባረከ 'was blessed' (passive-reflexive of ባረከ, cf. ባረኮ 'blessed him' in ch. 14). ሠነየ 'was fair, good'. ፋሬስ Perez (Genesis 38:29). From here the list of kings follows a formula: ወእምድኅሬሁ ነግሠ [name] ወልዱ — 'and after him reigned [name] his son'; I give it in full once and then nudge. The names follow the genealogy of Matthew 1 and Luke 3.

sentences.t: ውእቱኒ ፡ አዕረፈ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ኢሳሮም ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: He also rested, and-reigned Isarom his-son;
sentences.i: He too rested, and his son Hezron reigned;
sentences.n: ኢሳሮም is Hezron (Greek Esrom, Matthew 1:3). ውእቱኒ አዕረፈ 'he also reposed' (died). The ኦ/ኢ-initial forms in this list are the Ethiopic spellings of the names in the Greek lists.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ኦርኒ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Orni his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Arni reigned;
sentences.n: ኦርኒ: Arni of Luke 3:33 (the Greek genealogy has Arni between Hezron and Admin). Formula as above.

sentences.t: ወእም ፡ ድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ አራም ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Aram his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Aram reigned;
sentences.n: ወእም ፡ ድኅሬሁ is printed with a space between እም and ድኅሬሁ — one word split in the source (እምድኅሬሁ); I keep the source as is. አራም Aram (Matthew 1:3–4, Ram).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ አሚናዳብ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Amminadab his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Amminadab reigned;
sentences.n: አሚናዳብ Amminadab (Ruth 4:19; Matthew 1:4).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ነአሶን ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Nahshon his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Nahshon reigned;
sentences.n: ነአሶን Nahshon (Greek Naasson; Numbers 1:7).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ሳላ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Sala his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Salmon reigned;
sentences.n: ሳላ: the Sala/Salmon of the genealogies (Ruth 4:20, Matthew 1:4–5 have Salmon; Luke 3:32 has Sala). I give 'Salmon' in English as the conventional form of the name.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ባዖስ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Baos his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Boaz reigned;
sentences.n: ባዖስ: Boaz (Greek Booz, Ruth 4:21).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ኢዮቤድ ፡ ወልዱ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Iyobed his-son;
sentences.i: and after him his son Obed reigned;
sentences.n: ኢዮቤድ: Obed (Greek Iobed, Ruth 4:21).

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ እሴይ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ወመንግሥተ ፡ ዘእቤ ፡ በረከተ ፡ አብ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ወልድ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትባረክ ፡ በሠናይ ፤
sentences.l: and-after-him reigned Jesse his-son; and-the-kingdom which I-speak-of (is) blessing-of father upon son, that he-be-blessed in-good;
sentences.i: and after him his son Jesse reigned; and the kingdom I speak of is a father's blessing upon a son, that he may be blessed with what is good;
sentences.n: እሴይ Jesse, David's father. UNCERTAIN: ወመንግሥተ ዘእቤ — I read ዘእቤ as 'which I say (speak of)', an aside by the author, and the kingdom as the 'blessing of a father upon a son' (cf. Isaac blessing Jacob, Genesis 27). The grammar is loose: መንግሥተ is in the accusative with no verb, so the clause is possibly cut or elliptical. በረከተ አብ 'blessing-of father' (construct); ከመ ይትባረክ 'that he be blessed' (ከመ + subjunctive).

sentences.t: ወመንግሥትሰ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ሞተ ፡ እሴይ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ በጽድቅ ፡ ወበርትዕ ፡ ወበየውሀት ፨
sentences.l: And-the-kingdom indeed over Israel, after died Jesse, reigned David in-righteousness and-in-uprightness and-in-simplicity.
sentences.i: As for the kingdom over Israel, after Jesse died, David reigned in righteousness, uprightness, and simplicity.
sentences.n: መንግሥትሰ 'as for the kingdom' (topic with -ሰ). እምድኅረ ሞተ እሴይ 'after died Jesse' (verb before subject, the usual order). ነግሠ ዳዊት 'reigned David'. የውሀት 'gentleness, innocence' (cf. Psalm 78:72). ፨ ends the part.
